scope: Camera state, active-camera/viewer selection, view and projection, pointer-to-camera conversion, camera-mode input, attachment/follow semantics, world/local transform composition, gameplay-to-presentation transform submission, transformed bounds, and gameplay-relevant visibility culling. Renderer backend internals remain behind the render submission boundary.

boundaries.boundary: Active camera, viewer attachment, and camera-manager routing
boundaries.gameplay_caller: App mode setup and App::cCameraManager message dispatch; Cell steering later observes camera mode through the viewer/camera path
boundaries.original_callee: App::cCameraManager::SetActiveCamera, SetActiveCameraByID, SetViewer, HandleMessage, GetActiveCamera, and GetActiveCameraID
parameters: active camera object, numeric ID, key, or name
state_changed: camera ID/name maps and active-camera selection
boundaries.lifetime: The manager owns registered camera objects and names for application lifetime; the viewer attachment changes with mode setup or camera-service messages.
boundaries.failure_semantics: SetViewer is a trivial guard/forwarding method in the exported body and is not a follow-behavior implementation. SetActiveCameraByID returns a success flag; its named-string path throws after printing "No such camera" when the requested name is absent. Exact numeric-ID failure behavior is not fully established.
boundaries.timing_order: Initialize and populate the camera service, attach the stage viewer, select an active camera, handle camera-change messages, then expose active-camera state to stage and viewer updates.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Typed ICameraService and ICameraController with setViewer, setActiveCamera, activeCamera, and activeCameraId; injected into a mode rather than accessed through a global manager.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: ICameraService owns camera identity and selection, while ICameraTarget or ICameraController owns viewer attachment. Do not reproduce cCameraManager layouts, vtables, hash maps, or global service roots.

boundaries.boundary: Viewer view transform, projection, viewport, and render-update state
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Renderer frame setup, editor/camera setup, and Cell presentation initialization; pointer-to-world conversion later reads this camera state
boundaries.original_callee: App::cViewer::SetViewTransform, GetViewTransform, SetPerspectiveProjection, SetParallelProjection, SetViewOffset, SetViewWindow, SetAspectRatio, SetNearPlane, SetFarPlane, SetViewport, BeginUpdate, and EndUpdate
parameters: aspect ratio, viewport dimensions, and near/far planes
state_changed: camera viewport, view offset, view window, aspect, and clip planes
viewer update and main render-target bindings
boundaries.lifetime: Camera state follows the active viewer and target; render-update state follows a frame or layer, while main color/depth attachments follow renderer lifetime and resize.
boundaries.failure_semantics: SetViewTransform lazily creates the graphics state and returns without applying further camera setup if creation fails. Setter and anchor drift prevent a complete error contract; renderer initialization failure is presentation failure, not a demonstrated gameplay transition.
boundaries.timing_order: Set viewport and projection, update the camera/view transform, begin the viewer/render update, submit layer or model work, then end the update. The same projection/viewport values must be used by pointer-to-world conversion so gameplay rays agree with the rendered view.
boundaries.openspore_concept: ICameraState containing position, orientation, projection, viewport, and clip planes, plus ICameraController and IRenderer frame lifecycle methods.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: Use a backend-neutral CameraState and ProjectionState. Keep gameplay reads of projection/viewport coherent with rendering, but do not expose cViewer matrices, D3D viewport structs, or the 372-byte cViewer layout.

boundaries.boundary: Mouse-camera input, view-transform calculation, and camera-mode consumption

parameters: mouse-camera viewer and current camera state
outputs: calculated view transform used by later camera queries
boundaries.lifetime: Per input event and per camera update; the camera object persists while selected by the camera manager.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The exported OnKeyDown body is only a forwarding wrapper, and no persisted bodies exist for mouse move, wheel, CalculateViewTransform, or Update. Individual key, sensitivity, clamping, and consumption semantics are therefore unresolved.
boundaries.timing_order: Poll and route mouse/key/wheel events, update the selected camera, finalize its view transform, then run gameplay movement and presentation submission using the same camera state.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Input events update a typed CameraController; CameraState supplies the gameplay ray, while the renderer consumes the same view/projection snapshot.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IInputRouter plus ICameraController with pointerDelta, button, wheel, key, and update operations. Keep event ordering and normalized values, not the original virtual-key ABI or singleton.

boundaries.boundary: Camera follow target and viewer attachment semantics
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Cell camera origin/target and presentation follow behavior; gameplay steering uses the same camera state
boundaries.original_callee: The available evidence establishes App::cCameraManager::SetViewer and App::cViewer::SetViewTransform as attachment/render-state operations, but does not establish a distinct original follow-target method
parameters: camera offset, distance, yaw, and pitch
follow enablement and any smoothing parameters
outputs: view transform for rendering and pointer conversion
state_changed: derived camera position and view transform
boundaries.lifetime: Attachment follows the current mode/viewer; target follow state follows the target entity and is updated per frame when active.
boundaries.failure_semantics: No target, inactive camera mode, or unavailable viewer has no established original gameplay error. Current OpenSpore copies the player position directly into CameraState::target after gameplay integration, but that is a clean-room approximation rather than a recovered original follow contract.
boundaries.timing_order: A Cell steering query intentionally uses the prior frame's target; after movement/interactions, the current OpenSpore model copies the new player position into the camera target for the next render and next steering query.
boundaries.openspore_concept: CameraState::target and the end-of-update follow assignment; current CameraState::eyePos derives a follow-orbit eye.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: An optional ICameraTarget with attach/detach, setTargetTransform, and updateFollow; do not require follow if no gameplay behavior consumes it. Preserve one-frame ordering only where movement causality depends on it.

boundaries.boundary: World/local transform composition and conversion to a render matrix
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Cell/entity creation, model and terrain setup, editor world operations, and presentation effects compose gameplay-owned transforms
boundaries.original_callee: Transform::PreTransformBy and Transform::ToMatrix4; local transform math helpers
parameters: offset, quaternion or rotation matrix, and scale
boundaries.lifetime: Value lifetime; transforms are embedded in entities, properties, models, camera state, and presentation records and are copied when submitted.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The exported composition method has no typed error path. Decompiler helpers are evidence only, so invalid/denormal transform handling and exact normalization order are not established.
boundaries.timing_order: Compose or assign entity/local transforms during gameplay state construction, snapshot them after movement/animation, convert to a matrix at the presentation boundary, then submit draw state.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Typed local position/orientation/scale state and a renderer-facing affine transform; CellPool currently preserves the original 56-byte Transform slot as opaque bytes.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: Use a backend-neutral AffineTransform value with compose, inverse, transformPoint, and transformDirection operations. Preserve coordinate handedness and composition order, not Matrix3 storage or original flags.

boundaries.boundary: Gameplay entity transform to Cell GFX and renderer submission

boundaries.failure_semantics: Missing renderer, lighting, or effect services prevent presentation but do not establish a gameplay state transition. A bad transform can make submission invalid, but original validation/error propagation is not characterized.

boundaries.boundary: Transformed bounding boxes for models, terrain, and visibility tests

outputs: world-space bounds or radius suitable for a cull test

boundaries.lifetime: Bounds follow the model/terrain transform snapshot; cached world bounds are invalidated when the owning transform changes.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The exported method has no explicit failure path. Its decompiler output is too type-noisy to prove exact corner ordering, empty-volume behavior, or rotation-specific optimization semantics.
boundaries.timing_order: Compute local bounds with the asset/model, transform them after the authoritative world transform is final, then use the result for visibility or gameplay queries that explicitly require world bounds.
boundaries.openspore_concept: assets::Mesh carries bboxMin, bboxMax, and radius; gameplay proximity/query state is separate from renderer culling.

boundaries.boundary: Projection-derived frustum planes and sphere/AABB visibility culling
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Cell per-frame update refreshes cull state, and editor/terrain/model passes test bounds; no reviewed caller uses the cull result to gate a Cell gameplay transition
parameters: world bounds center, half extents, or radius
boundaries.lifetime: Planes are a frame/view snapshot; the cull object itself follows renderer or camera-state lifetime.
boundaries.failure_semantics: Exact plane extraction and return-value polarity are not trustworthy in the available FrustumTestSphere decompilation. No gameplay failure path is established if a test reports outside.
boundaries.timing_order: Finalize projection/view state, update the six planes, transform or select world bounds, test visibility, then skip or submit affected presentation work. The Cell update body calls the update routine, but downstream gameplay use of its result is not established.
boundaries.openspore_concept: OpenSpore currently culls dead scene entities before draw and otherwise relies on the rasterizer; it has no shared gameplay visibility state.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: ICamera::frustum plus a presentation VisibilitySet or renderer-level bounds test. If future gameplay uses visibility, expose a separately named semantic query rather than sharing the render cull bit implicitly.

unresolved: No positive original Cell-mode runtime trace exists, so camera-mode values, pointer causality, movement-plane runtime point, frame ordering, and follow behavior remain static-only conclusions.
The exact original matrix handedness, projection/depth convention, default FOV, near/far values, aspect handling, and GetCameraToMouse unprojection formula are not runtime-observed.

GetCameraToPoint, GetCameraToMouse, SetPerspectiveProjection, Transform::ToMatrix4, and two cFrustumCull SDK anchors lie inside larger live Ghidra functions; exact sub-boundaries require a read-only decompiler capture when the project lock is available.

App::cMouseCamera::OnMouseMove, OnMouseWheel, CalculateViewTransform, and Update have SDK/vtable evidence but no persisted bodies, so sensitivity, clamping, zoom, smoothing, and event-consumption rules are unresolved.
The camera-mode word at the Cell camera structure offset +0xd4 and its UI-selection gates are not characterized.
No distinct original follow-target or attach/detach method is established. OpenSpore's end-of-update target copy and orbit formula are inferred/approximated, not recovered semantics.

The exact transformed-BoundingBox corner algorithm and FrustumTestSphere return polarity are decompiler-noisy; preserve typed world bounds and an explicit cull result rather than original field behavior.

The Cell per-frame body refreshes cull state, but no reviewed path proves that visibility gates movement, interaction, spawning, or other gameplay state; culling remains presentation-only unless new evidence establishes a gameplay consumer.

Renderer backend implementation details remain owned by the D3D/RenderWare boundary; this report freezes only the camera/transform values, coordinate conversions, and submission ordering needed by gameplay and presentation.
